answer: Give every new identity a slow-release trust budget: it must stake a bond that unlocks only gradually, like a glacier moving, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds while honest work accrues usable reputation over weeks. One cedar-like root identity, verified once through a costly checkable anchor, may vouch for newcomers, but its vouching power is capped and slashed if any vouched identity cheats. At the dawn of each epoch, payouts weight long-lived, vouched identities far above fresh ones, so sybils arrive too late and too expensive to matter.
